clue.text: Man to do in for being a trespasser?

parts.note: a man is a male
a factor is an agent, someone who does business in place of another; read loosely, one who acts in for someone

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man killed for trespassing deserved it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do in' suggests killing, but the phrase points to an agent acting on another's behalf. The question mark flags the old sense of trespass as sin, so a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser in the biblical sense is a sinner or wrongdoer, which is what a criminal offender is.

clue.text: Scot dealing with wine

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Scotsman in the wine trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Burgundy wine, red or white, named after a town in the Saone valley.

clue.text: At any rate, it was original point, in general

indicators.note: the anagram and the point go inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

indicators.note: original in the sense of novel, so the words it was appear in a new form

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a point was at least original in general terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges IT WAS into ASTWI; with S after it, 'in' puts the run inside LEE, the American Civil War general.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning at least or in any case, a hedge on a statement.

clue.text: Advice from Times in playful imitation

explanation.surface: A newspaper urges readers to copy it.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a newspaper's editorial, so The Times might advise readers to follow its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which everyone copies the moves of the one in front; and a paper's editorial telling readers to heed it.

clue.text: Droop in the centre of the bouquet

indicators.note: the word for droop goes in the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre
to droop is to sag

explanation.surface: The flowers in the middle of the arrangement are wilting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of the bouquet' looks like a single phrase, but 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spray of flowers worn on a dress or wrist at a formal occasion.

clue.text: Manage to give love-poetry point

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
verse is poetry
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make love poetry pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct something is to be in charge of its running.

clue.text: Try wallop for party

explanation.surface: Someone reaches for a beating as the answer to a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Have a go, a heavy blow and a lively celebration are all colloquial senses of one short word.

clue.text: Region containing many a palm tree

indicators.note: the region word holds the numeral within it

parts.note: an area is a region
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: An area with many palms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives C, the Roman numeral 100.
explanation.definitionFit: An Asian palm genus that yields the betel nut.

clue.text: Not altogether right, like "The Two Feathers"?

explanation.surface: A slightly wrong title quoted from a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel and film are The Four Feathers, so The Two Feathers is half the name; a half claim to something is only part of a right.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial claim is only part of a legal right; and the short page before a book's main title page bears its name alone.

clue.text: Getting unique impression of typist's job?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a keyboard worker's job leaves a distinctive mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A typist prints with the fingers, hence the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Police take each person's distinctive whorl marks as identification; and a typist produces type by hand.

clue.text: Obsequious swimmer?

parts.note: a fawning, toadying person is a sycophant; a swimmer may also do the front stroke called the crawl

explanation.surface: A grovelling person seen as someone in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who fawns is said to grovel, and a swimmer doing front crawl is literally one, so both senses fit.

clue.text: E.g. a pile may be growing above ground

indicators.note: the letters of the three words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A heap of something, perhaps a compost pile, sprouting upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals rearranging EG, A and PILE into this botanical adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for cotyledons or plants that develop above the soil surface rather than beneath it.

clue.text: Reform — not, alas, in country folk

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that reform has not reached rural people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country folk' suggests rustics, but it means citizens of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens belonging to a particular nation are its subjects or members, the people of that state.

clue.text: Make allowances for old lady, sort of square

parts.note: gran is a familiar name for a grandmother
a T-square is a drafting instrument

explanation.surface: Someone advises being lenient with an elderly woman who is rather old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of square' looks like 'rather fuddy-duddy' about the old lady, but it is the T of a T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede or admit a point is to allow it, making allowance for it in argument.

clue.text: Blame for platform not opening

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the word for platform is dropped

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker's stage is blamed for staying shut.
explanation.definitionFit: General hatred and opprobrium directed at someone, the disgrace or censure that attaches to them.

clue.text: Unpleasant death in part beyond roads

indicators.note: the word for death goes in the stretch of sea

parts.note: the offing is the stretch of sea visible beyond the roads, a sheltered anchorage
end means death

explanation.surface: A nasty fatality somewhere past the highways.
explanation.walkthrough: Roads here is a roadstead, an anchorage off shore, not streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives offence is disagreeable or distasteful.

clue.text: Military command put watches correct

parts.note: to watch something is to eye it
correct means right

explanation.surface: Someone orders that timepieces be set accurately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watches' reads as wristwatches, but it is the verb: eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade-ground order telling marching troops to turn their heads towards the saluting dais.

clue.text: Silly fellow has to pay for a plant

parts.note: a goose is a silly person
to foot the bill is to pay for it

explanation.surface: A fool has to fund a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory, but it is a weed of the spinach family.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of the beet family, named for its webbed leaves.

clue.text: Sort of writer, slippery type Anatole caught

indicators.note: the novelist's surname has caught the slippery creature, holding it inside

parts.note: Anatole France was a French novelist
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A slippery author named Anatole is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts EEL inside FRANCE, the surname of the novelist Anatole France.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed journalist who sells work to many publications rather than holding a staff post.

clue.text: Pile that almost absorbs hot inflammable oil

indicators.note: the pile and shortened word take in the letter for hot

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on fabric

indicators.note: almost means the word that loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A heap that soaks up heat turns into fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THAT to THA; 'absorbs' puts H into NAPTHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile flammable liquid hydrocarbon distilled from petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: Men rise as ordered, as judges appear in them

indicators.note: as ordered means put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Men stand when judges enter court in their robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ordered' rearranges MEN RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: White winter fur of the stoat, used to trim the robes of judges and peers.

clue.text: Right edge of river

parts.note: to edge a blade is to sharpen or hone it

explanation.surface: The right bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge' looks like a noun (riverbank), but it is the verb: to sharpen.
explanation.definitionFit: A major European waterway rising in the Swiss Alps and flowing through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Girl's inconclusive sort of conquest

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: inconclusive means without its conclusion, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the Norman Conquest of England in 1066

explanation.surface: A girl's romantic conquest that never quite ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conquest' suggests romance, but it is the Norman Conquest of 1066 with its last letter cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the opera heroine or Norma Jean.

clue.text: In fitter state, runs one through

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one
per means through or by

explanation.surface: Someone runs one through while in better condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit further on the way to maturity is more ready for eating.

clue.text: Thinks about surrounding mummy with aromatic spheres

indicators.note: the word for thinks about goes around the word for mummy

parts.note: to think about is to ponder, here third person
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone deliberates over an Egyptian mummy surrounded by scented balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' looks Egyptian, but it is mother: MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforated balls of perfume or fragrant herbs once carried to ward off smells and infection.

clue.text: Service in which sub appears

explanation.surface: A church service in which a substitute takes part.
explanation.walkthrough: Service is the old sense of benefit, as in standing someone in good stead.
explanation.definitionFit: Usefulness or advantage; and in place of another, so a substitute is there instead.

clue.text: Naughty child, to lie in earnest

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to rest is to lie down

explanation.surface: A naughty child is told seriously to lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in earnest' reads as seriously, but 'in' is a link and 'earnest' is the noun: a deposit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid in advance as a pledge, a loan or advance given to secure a contract.

clue.text: The best part of what is offensive

parts.note: the best is number one, written No 1 and read as NOI
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Someone singles out the worst part of something objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The best' is No 1, the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul-smelling or disgusting, unpleasant and objectionable to the senses.

clue.text: Small confection of spice, sugar etc.

definitions.text: Small confection of spice, sugar etc.

parts.words: Small confection of spice, sugar etc.
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says little females are made of sugar and spice and all things nice

explanation.surface: A tiny sweet made of spices and sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'What are little boys made of?' answers that little daughters are made of sugar and spice and all things nice.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme describes young females as made of sugar and spice, so a little one is that confection.

clue.text: Prudent as Alice, seeing nobody?

explanation.surface: A sensible Alice looks down the road and sees no one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass Alice says she sees nobody on the road, and the King envies eyes that can see Nobody at that distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent means planning wisely for the future; seeing Nobody far off would need long-distance vision.
